subject: Maths
title: Basic probability — single events
subtitle: Probability · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can calculate the probability of a single event using fractions.

key_vocab.definition: Probability measures how likely something is to happen, from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain). It equals favourable outcomes ÷ total outcomes.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can calculate the probability of a single event using fractions.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Basic probability -- Probability measures how likely something is to happen, from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain). It equals favourable outcomes ÷ total outcomes.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Probability = favourable outcomes divided by total equally likely outcomes.
P(event) = &frac{favourable}{total}
Always a value between 0 and 1

Key examples:
  ✓ P(heads on a coin) = &frac{1}{2}  (1 out of 2 outcomes)
  ✓ P(6 on a die) = &frac{1}{6}  (1 out of 6 outcomes)
  ✓ P(not A) = 1 - P(A)  (complementary events)
  ✗ P(heads) = &frac{1}{3} because heads, tails, or edge  (edge is not equally likely)
  ✗ P(6 on a die) = &frac{1}{3} because even or odd or 6  (wrong outcomes)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – single die
  A fair six-sided die is rolled. Find P(even number).
  Even numbers: 2, 4, 6 (3 outcomes)
  Total outcomes: 6
  P(even) = &frac{3}{6} = &frac{1}{2}
  = &frac{1}{2}
  (Count the favourable outcomes and divide by total.)

Example 2 – bag of sweets
  A bag has 3 red, 5 blue, and 2 green sweets. Find P(blue).
  Favourable (blue): 5
  Total: 3 + 5 + 2 = 10
  P(blue) = &frac{5}{10} = &frac{1}{2}
  = &frac{1}{2}
  (Add all sweets for the total, then simplify.)

sections.title: Dice probabilities
sections.content:
A fair six-sided die is rolled. Find each probability.

(a) P(3)
(b) P(odd)
(c) P(greater than 4)
(d) P(less than 5)

sections.title: Bag probabilities
sections.content:
A bag has 4 red, 6 blue, and 5 green balls. Find each probability.

(a) P(red)
(b) P(blue)
(c) P(green)
(d) P(not red)

sections.title: Complementary probabilities
sections.content:
Use P(not A) = 1 - P(A).

(a) P(win) = 0.6. Find P(not win)
(b) P(late) = &frac{1}{5}. Find P(not late)
(c) P(rain) = 0.35. Find P(no rain)
(d) P(pass) = &frac{7}{10}. Find P(fail)

sections.title: Spinners and cards
sections.content:
Find each probability.

(a) A card from a pack of 52: P(heart)
(b) A card from a pack of 52: P(king)
(c) Spinner 1-10: P(multiple of 3)
(d) Spinner 1-10: P(square number)

sections.title: Mixed single event probability
sections.content:
Calculate each probability as a simplified fraction.

(a) Letter from MATHEMATICS: P(vowel)
(b) Number 1-20: P(factor of 12)
(c) Bag: 7 red, 3 blue. P(blue) after adding 2 blue
(d) Die: P(prime or 1)
(e) P(A) = x. P(not A) in terms of x

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ P(event) is always between 0 and 1
✗ If you flip a coin 10 times you will always get 5 heads
✓ P(not A) = 1 - P(A)
✗ A probability of 0.5 means the event is certain
✓ P(6 on a fair die) = &frac{1}{6}
